{"parentUuid":"152eb96a-0360-4a4d-a1ca-2a960754c38b","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"skill_listing","content":"- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors (\"from now on when X\", \"each time X\", \"whenever X\", \"before/after X\") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: \"rebind ctrl+s\", \"add a chord shortcut\", \"change the submit key\", \"customize keybindings\".\n- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.\n- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.\n- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).\nTRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.\nSKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.\n- ccs-delegation: Auto-activate CCS CLI delegation for deterministic tasks. Parses user input, auto-selects optimal profile (glm/kimi/custom) from ~/.ccs/config.json, enhances prompts with context, executes via `ccs {profile} -p \"task\"` or `ccs {profile}:continue`, and reports results. Triggers on \"use ccs [task]\" patterns, typo/test/refactor keywords. Excludes complex architecture, security-critical code, performance optimization, breaking changes.\n- attach: Port the Claude Code harness layer from this project to a new project directory. Use when bootstrapping a fresh Claude Code project on the same machine, when peers want to copy the harness, or when verifying layer separation via dry-run. Reads .claude/manifest.yaml; copies harness-tagged artifacts only; excludes stockforge biz + personal layers; generates skeleton CLAUDE.md + manifest at target.\n- crawler-reliability: Build reliable web crawlers for data gathering. Use when implementing scrapers for CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz, YouTube (yt-dlp), Facebook fanpages, or any external data source. Covers Python/Playwright patterns, retry/backoff, selector robustness, rate limiting, monitoring.\n- ddd-tactical-patterns: Apply DDD tactical patterns (aggregate, entity, value object, repository, domain event, anti-corruption layer) correctly in Python/dataclasses code. Use when designing or implementing domain models, repositories, or cross-bounded-context communication in StockForge's 9 BCs.\n- decompose-work: Split a non-trivial task into deterministic-vs-LLM portions before execution. Use when planning multi-step work where some sub-tasks are mechanical (file ops, regex, count, schema validation) and others require judgment (synthesis, design, ambiguity resolution). Outputs structured plan that maps each portion to the cheapest competent tool. Pairs with capability-map.md (model × effort × task_class grounding) and try-n-approaches (S9 — Karpathy autoresearch loop).\n- evidence-extraction: Extract structured claims from unstructured sources with citation integrity. Use when building extraction pipelines, parsing news articles or KOL transcripts, or anywhere claims are created from raw data. Ensures every claim has source_url, extracted_at, confidence, and verified attribution. Enforces no-LLM-math invariant (I-S1).\n- fastapi-module: Implement FastAPI routers following StockForge conventions. Use when creating a new HTTP endpoint, adding routes, wiring dependency injection, configuring Pydantic DTOs. Covers router boundaries, provider patterns, testing setup. Phase 2+ only — Phase 1 uses Streamlit dashboard directly.\n- grill-maximization: Doctrine for bundling Q&A questions to the human at maximum density per turn (15-20 target, max 25), so each human-in-the-loop touchpoint is information-rich. Use when composing a Q&A bundle for human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, or when deciding whether to ask one question or wait and bundle. Built on the principle that human-in-the-loop time is the scarcest resource in autonomous coding.\n- obsidian-vault: Search, create, and manage notes in the StockForge Obsidian vault with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index maintenance. Use when adding content to the knowledge base, navigating entities/concepts, or maintaining the raw/wiki separation. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed. Extended with raw/wiki pattern from Karpathy LLM Wiki.\n- postgres-pgvector: Design Postgres schemas with pgvector and TimescaleDB for StockForge. Use when creating migrations, designing tables, writing queries. Covers vector embeddings for semantic search on Vietnamese text, time-series for price/sentiment data, JSONB vs structured columns.\n- promote-rule: Cluster agent-notes.md entries by lexical similarity, propose promotion of recurring rules to deterministic hook (priority 1), skill (priority 2), or charter (priority 3). Use when agent-notes has accumulated ≥10 new rules since last promotion run, or on-demand at phase boundary. Outputs proposal markdown to observations/. Pairs with capability-map.md (writes new task_class entries) and decompose-work (consumes promotion outcomes).\n- prompt-engineering: Design and optimize LLM prompts for StockForge pipeline stages. Use when writing or refining prompts for claim extraction, KOL recommendation extraction, sentiment analysis, thesis synthesis. Covers context assembly, prompt caching strategy, budget-aware prompts, structured output. Enforces no-LLM-math constraint.\n- qa-escalation: File-based Q&A protocol — composes bundle file in human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/, tracks lifecycle (pending → answered → stale → processed), creates URGENT notification when needed. Use when intent classifier recommends OPEN_QA_BUNDLE / ESCALATE_HUMAN, or grill-maximization has a bundle ready to write. Pairs with grill-maximization (composes content) + Track 5 hooks (auto-move stale).\n- spec-dual-layer: Write specifications with dual-layer structure (business narrative + agent contract). Use when authoring new specs, refining existing specs, or understanding the spec template. Ensures both human stakeholder needs and agent execution needs are served.\n- spec-to-wiki: Convert raw specifications to Obsidian wiki format with wikilinks, frontmatter, and index updates. Use when adding a new spec to the knowledge base, or when regenerating wiki view after spec changes. Maintains raw as source of truth, wiki as navigable view.\n- test-pyramid-balance: Balance unit, integration, and E2E tests properly in Python/pytest. Use when deciding what test to write, reviewing test coverage, or rebalancing skewed test suite. Covers test pyramid shape, BDD vs unit tests, when to use what. Includes stock-domain-specific test categories.\n- ubiquitous-language: Extract a DDD-style ubiquitous language glossary from the current conversation or domain area. Use when starting work on a new bounded context, when new domain terms emerge, or when verifying consistency between business language and code. Adapted from mattpocock/skills, MIT licensed.\n- user-prompt-intake: Hybrid intent classifier — main session lite-detects trivial prompts, dispatches intent-classifier subagent for complex ones. Use whenever a new user prompt lands (chat or file in human-workspace/user_prompt/) and you need to route the work. Built for full-autonomous loop where every prompt must be classified before action.\n- write-a-skill: Create new Claude Code skills with proper structure, progressive disclosure, and discoverability. Use when extracting a pattern from multiple sessions into a reusable skill, or when user asks to formalize a technique. After 12-24 months of dogfood, the system should be a genuine advisor I would pay money for if someone else built it.\n17\t\n18\tNot a goal: high-frequency trading, replacing human judgment, becoming a SaaS in Year 1, beating frontier LLMs at general reasoning, providing licensed financial advice.\n19\t\n20\t---\n21\t\n22\t## The Core Insight (the why)\n23\t\n24\t**Quant funds (Renaissance, Two Sigma, DE Shaw) win in efficient markets through clean data + execution speed + diverse alpha factors.** They don't use sentiment from Facebook/YouTube because at their scale it's noise, not signal — and in efficient markets it gets arbitraged away anyway.\n25\t\n26\t**Vietnam stock market inverts this.** It is structurally inefficient:\n27\t- 85-90% retail investor share (vs 20-25% in US)\n28\t- Information asymmetry between sophisticated and retail crowd\n29\t- KOL/influencer recommendations measurably move prices\n30\t- \"Đội lái\" (pump operators) operate openly\n31\t- News and narrative cycles dominate over fundamentals for months at a time\n32\t- Foreign flow creates non-fundamental price pressure\n33\t\n34\tIn this market, **sentiment + influence + narrative tracking is signal, not noise**. And LLMs can process Vietnamese unstructured text at scale that was impossible before 2023.\n35\t\n36\tThis creates a **structural arbitrage**: apply quant methodology + LLM reasoning + sentiment/influence data layers that no commercial product offers for VN. Position not as \"decision maker\" but as **advisor + alert watcher + bias mirror**.\n37\t\n38\t---\n39\t\n40\t## The Craft Philosophy\n41\t\n42\tTake the craft seriously. Build for personal use first, commercial second.\n43\t\n44\t- Production-grade engineering standards from Day 1 (DDD + clean architecture + multi-loop discipline)\n45\t- Commercial extension kept as option, never as driver\n46\t- When self-use conflicts with hypothetical-future-SaaS, self-use wins\n47\t- Quality bar: I genuinely trust output enough to act on real money decisions\n48\t- Edge comes from compounding moats (proprietary data, calibration, personal bias log), not from any single feature\n49\t\n50\tReference models: Renaissance Technologies (data + iteration discipline), Bridgewater (principles-based decision making), personal Bloomberg Terminal (data density + analysis depth), Athletic.com (subscription-quality content for niche audience).\n51\t\n52\t---\n53\t\n54\t## Core Principles (non-negotiable)\n55\t\n56\t1. **Evidence grounding** — every claim, every number traceable to source + as-of date. Hallucination in finance = bug, not stylistic issue.\n57\t\n58\t2. **Structured output over narrative** — multi-criteria assessment, never single \"buy/sell\" score. Output is trade-off matrix.\n59\t\n60\t3. **Adversarial by design** — bear + bull + critic + quant + behavior + manager perspectives. Never consensus from single agent.\n61\t\n62\t4. **Proprietary data moat** — every news ingested, every KOL recommendation tracked, every thesis post-mortem'd compounds the edge. Raw data is sacred.\n63\t\n64\t5. **Pattern transfer + local adaptation** — global setups (cyclical bottom, dividend value, GARP) + Vietnam-specific overlays (policy timing, foreign flow, narrative phase).\n65\t\n66\t6. **Human-in-loop is the product** — augment thinking, never replace it. System should challenge user's gut instinct without overriding it.\n67\t\n68\t7. **Dogfood mandatory** — if I don't use it weekly for real decisions, the feature gets killed. Self-use is the only validation that matters in Year 1.\n69\t\n70\t8. **Calibration over confidence** — system tracks its own accuracy across signal types, never claims confidence it hasn't earned through hit rate.\n71\t\n72\t9. **No LLM math** — LLM never generates numbers. All calculations through deterministic code with verified data inputs. LLM only interprets.\n73\t\n74\t10. **Position sizing & risk management are deterministic** — code-enforced rules, LLM cannot override. Maximum position size, sector concentration, stop loss rules are immutable per session.\n75\t\n76\t---\n77\t\n78\t## The Four-Tier Signal Architecture\n79\t\n80\tSystem operates on four distinct signal tiers, each with different lead time, reliability, and processing approach:\n81\t\n82\t**Tier 1 — Hard Data (deterministic):** prices, volumes, fundamentals, foreign flow, macro indicators. Zero LLM, pure code. Lead time: hours-days.\n83\t\n84\t**Tier 2 — Official Narrative (semi-structured):** mainstream financial news, broker reports, official company disclosures, government announcements. LLM extracts claims + classifies sentiment + detects contradictions. Lead time: real-time.\n85\t\n86\t**Tier 3 — Influence Network (semi-structured):** YouTube channels, Facebook KOL pages, Telegram channels, podcasts. LLM transcribes + extracts recommendations + tags entities. Calibration database tracks each KOL's accuracy over time. Lead time: can lead by days.\n87\t\n88\t**Tier 4 — Crowd Sentiment & Pump Detection (unstructured):** community forums, public chat groups, comments. LLM classifies sentiment + detects coordinated posting + identifies pump narratives + tracks narrative lifecycle phase. diverge?\n- 3-5 trusted peers using it, providing feedback\n- Demonstrable alpha vs VN-Index on dogfood portfolio (or honest accounting of why not)\n\n**Ultimate signal of success**: When my gut says \"buy XYZ\", I check what StockForge says first — and seriously consider it when it disagrees.\n\n---\n\n## Technical Foundation (locked Phase 1-3)\n\n**Stack:**\n- **Python primary** — for data science, LLM workflows, time-series, backtesting (heavier than IdeaForge which was TS-primary)\n- **Postgres 16 + TimescaleDB + pgvector + pg_trgm** — single DB for time-series + relational + vector\n- **Redis** — cache + pub/sub + queue broker\n- **Cloudflare R2** — raw content storage (PDFs, transcripts, scraped pages)\n- **Claude API primary** — Sonnet for most tasks, Opus for thesis synthesis\n- **OpenAI embeddings** — text-embedding-3-small (Vietnamese acceptable)\n- **NestJS** — only if/when we need a public-facing API (Phase 4+)\n- **Streamlit/Next.js** — Streamlit for personal dashboard (Phase 1-2), Next.js if SaaS path\n- **Apache Airflow / Prefect** — data pipeline orchestration\n\n**Architecture:**\n- Clean Architecture with DDD tactical patterns (same as IdeaForge)\n- 9 bounded contexts (see `agent-workspace/constitution/architecture.md`)\n- Event-driven for cross-context communication\n- Multi-loop execution (Karpathy outer + Continuous middle + Per-stock inner)\n\n**Development approach:**\n- AI-first: Claude Code as primary builder, human as spec author + reviewer + bias-checker\n- Spec-Driven (SDD) + Domain-Driven (DDD) + selective BDD\n- Sandwich pattern (Architect → Dev → Verifier) from Day 1\n- Verify-Before-Write (VBW) protocol mandatory\n- Three-tier quality gates (deterministic / probabilistic / human)\n\n---\n\n## Data Sources (Tier 1 budget)\n\n**Free/cheap (Phase 1):**\n- vnstock (open source) — historical EOD, fundamentals\n- Vietstock public — financial reports\n- TCBS API — semi-public market data\n- CafeF, NDH, VietnamBiz — news scraping\n- Public YouTube channels — transcript via yt-dlp + Whisper\n- Public Facebook fanpages — selective scraping (legal grey, careful scope)\n\n**Paid (Phase 2-3 if budget allows):**\n- FiinPro Platform — comprehensive fundamental data (~30-100M VND/year)\n- Wichart — pre-cleaned data\n- SSI FastConnect — realtime quotes if needed\n\n**Budget cap Year 1**: 50M VND for data + LLM combined.\n\n---\n\n## Meta-Discipline\n\nThese charter principles override daily decisions:\n\n- **When in doubt, simplify** — minimum code that solves the problem, nothing speculative\n- **Ship thin slices, not perfect systems** — each phase ends with something I actually use\n- **Document what you learn, not what you plan** — post-mortem > prospective docs\n- **Dogfood or delete** — features I don't use weekly get removed\n- **Calibrate, don't guess** — every confidence claim must have outcome tracking\n- **Stay agnostic about commercial outcome** — build for the craft, not for the exit\n\n---\n\n## Revision Protocol\n\nThis charter changes only when:\n- A core principle proves materially wrong through 30+ hours of real use\n- Scope demonstrably needs revision based on accumulated dogfood data\n- Technical foundation invalidated by external event (tool deprecation, regulatory change, etc.)\n\nCharter revisions require:\n- Written rationale with evidence (linked to specific sessions/post-mortems)\n- 48-hour cool-down before committing change\n- Explicit version bump (v1.0 → v2.0)\n\nMinor clarifications go in `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md`. This charter stays stable.\n\n---\n\n## Document Index\n\n| Document | Purpose | Stability |\n|---|---|---|\n| `PROJECT_CHARTER.md` (this) | Vision + principles | Immutable for ~3 months |\n| `AGENT_OPERATING_MANUAL.md` | Agent configs, skills, workflows | Living, frequent updates |\n| `SPEC_TEMPLATE.md` | How to write specs | Stable |\n| `specs/tier1-strategic/001-four-tier-signal-architecture.md` | Strategic: signal architecture | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/001-validate-investment-thesis.md` | First implementation spec | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/002-influence-network-tracking.md` | KOL tracking system spec | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/003-crowd-sentiment-pump-detection.md` | Pump detection spec | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/004-multi-perspective-adversarial-agents.md` | Adversarial analysis spec | Stable |\n| `specs/tier2-feature/005-karpathy-outer-loop.md` | Pipeline self-optimization spec | Stable |\n| `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` | Current state | Continuously updated |\n| `agent-workspace/memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules | Append-mostly |\n| `agent-workspace/memory/thesis-log/` | All thesis ever recorded | Append-only |\n| `agent-workspace/memory/post-mortems/` | Thesis outcome reviews | Append-only |\n| `agent-workspace/calibration/` | KOL accuracy, signal calibration data | Continuously updated |\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Charter (what we explicitly reject)\n\nTo stay focused, we reject these tempting paths:\n\n- **Predict prices with ML models** — models trained on VN price data overfit; no edge there.\n- **Compete with broker research** — we have less data, less staff. We win on integration + edge sources, not on raw analysis depth.\n- **Build for general retail public** — we build for ourselves and 3-5 peers. Mass market needs hand-holding we won't provide.\n- **Trust LLM for numbers** — every numerical output must come from code with traceable inputs.\n- **Build features without dogfooding** — speculative features die fast in this project.\n- **Optimize for backtest performance** — Goodhart's Law is real. We optimize for forward decision quality.\n- **Make money fast** — this is a 24-month project minimum to reach edge. {"parentUuid":"67df2576-a51a-4323-84b8-93d970379123","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"nested_memory","path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md","content":{"path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md","type":"Project","content":"# agent-workspace/ — Contract\n\n> **Audience**: agents working inside `agent-workspace/`.\n> **Established**: Decision 002 § Track 1 (Workspace Dualism Foundation).\n\n## Identity\n\n`agent-workspace/` is the **agent-owned execution + memory** layer. Everything here represents **agent state, decisions, plans, observations, learning**. Agents WRITE here freely (within constitution rules); humans READ here but normally do not edit.\n\nThis separation exists to prevent two failure modes from orch:\n1. **Charter drift via shared-workspace mutation** (orch CF-DOGFOOD-2)\n2. **Human cognitive overload from dense session logs** (UP02 §1.3 — \"human đối mặt hàng chục spec/document quá tải nếu không sắp xếp khoa học\")\n\nThe agent owns this directory but must keep it AUDITABLE — every artifact provenance-linked, every decision sourced.\n\n---\n\n## Subdirectories\n\n| Path | Purpose | Lifecycle |\n|---|---|---|\n| `constitution/` | **IMMUTABLE without explicit user approval**. Charter-tier rules (autonomous-protocol, model-routing, identity-scope, etc.). Track 7 produces drafts in `proposals/`; user explicit approve to move here. | Edit denied by .claude/settings.json; Write only via human approval gate |\n| `memory/project.md` | High-level project state; phase tracker; ADRs (last 5). Update on phase boundaries + architectural decisions. | Long-lived; trim to most recent decisions |\n| `memory/current-execution.md` | **THE single routing source of truth**. Active phase + active session + autonomous_mode flag + routing table. Read FIRST every session. | Long-lived; updated each session boundary |\n| `memory/agent-notes.md` | Learned rules from real experience (post-mortem / drift / user correction). Append-only mostly. | Long-lived |\n| `memory/decisions/` | Sequential ADRs (`NNN-<slug>.md`) + `_template.md` + `README.md` index. 12-field schema (Track 2). | Append-only; supersession via status field |\n| `memory/sessions/` | One file per session: `YYYY-MM-DD-session-N.md`. What happened, decisions made, files touched. | Append-only |\n| `memory/observations/` | Subagent return artifacts (per Track 6 spec). Each subagent writes one observation file describing what it did. | Append; cleaned periodically by aggregator |\n| `memory/checkpoints/` | Session handoff state for self-reboot (Track 5). `latest.md` is canonical pointer; timestamped historical files retained. | Append + latest.md updated each checkpoint |\n| `memory/patterns-discovered/` | Pattern mining outputs (Track 0 — DONE) + ongoing pattern catalog. | Append; significant patterns promoted to constitution |\n| `memory/drift-logs/` | Drift-check (DR1-DR12) results; runs on hook + on-demand. | Time-series append |\n| `memory/post-mortems/` | After significant failure or thesis-revoked event: what failed, root cause, prevention rule. | Append |\n| `memory/thesis-log/` | Stock-domain thesis exploration entries. Read-only for IMPL sessions. | Append + revisited per calibration |\n| `memory/sync-tracker/` | Track 8a output: Confidence Score SQLite + weights.yaml + auto-rendered `_index.md`. | Live updated by hooks |\n| `memory/self-awareness/` | Track 9 output: model × effort × thinking profile cards + known-issues + best-practices. | Live updated by Stop-hook aggregator |\n| `memory/mistake-log.md` | Track 7 deliverable: structured failure catalog. What went wrong / Root cause / Prevention rule / Severity. | Append; pre-flight read by all agents |\n| `session-plans/pending/` | Plans authored, awaiting execution. Phase 0 plan lives here. | Move to `completed/` when done |\n| `session-plans/completed/` | Executed plans; archived for reference + retrospective input. | Append |\n| `quality-reports/{deterministic,probabilistic,drift-reports}/` | Tier-1/2/3 gate outputs (CLAUDE.md § Quality Gates). | Per-run files |\n| `ubiquitous-language/` | DDD glossary + domain-mapping + drift-log. Stockforge stock-domain vocabulary. | Append; canonical via `/drill-me` |\n| `calibration/` | Empirical hit-rate data per signal type. Confidence claims MUST trace here (CLAUDE.md hard rule). | Append per thesis post-mortem |\n| `research/` | Research notes from `research-scanner` subagent dispatches (e.g., reference-repo studies). | Append |\n\n---\n\n## Contract Rules (BINDING)\n\n1. **Constitution is immutable absent explicit human approval.** `Edit/Write` to `agent-workspace/constitution/**` is in `.claude/settings.json` deny list. Track 7 writes constitution drafts to `proposals/`; user explicit approve moves them.\n\n2. **`memory/decisions/` is append-mostly + supersession-status.** Don't delete decisions; mark `status: superseded-by-D-NNN` to revoke. Sequential numbering (`001`, `002`, ...) — don't reuse numbers.\n\n3. **`current-execution.md` is the routing source-of-truth.** No skill, agent, or command may hardcode phase paths or session paths from memory; resolve via this file. Stale paths in CLAUDE.md or skills = anti-pattern.\n\n4. **Never edit `obsidian-vault/raw/`.** Immutable. Vault writes only to `wiki/`. (Established in stockforge CLAUDE.md.)\n\n5. **Provenance is mandatory.** Every decision file references its source (human prompt / spec clause / drift detection / agent inference). Every thesis cites source + as-of date (I-S2). Every confidence claim cites historical hit rate (I-S20-equivalent).\n\n6. **Agents never `git commit` in this directory unless user explicitly requests.** Stage only.\n\n7. **`patterns-discovered/` artifacts are READ-ONLY for production code.** Patterns must be promoted to constitution / skills / hook scripts before becoming binding. (Otherwise they're informal notes, not contracts.)\n\n---\n\n## Reading Priority for Agent\n\nPer `agent-workspace/constitution/autonomous-protocol.md` (Track 7) and stockforge `CLAUDE.md` § Session Protocol:\n\n1. **`memory/current-execution.md`** — first; resolve active track\n2. **`memory/project.md`** — project state\n3. **`memory/checkpoints/latest.md`** if a recent checkpoint exists (within last 24h) — resume context\n4. **`memory/agent-notes.md`** — learned rules\n5. **`memory/mistake-log.md`** — pre-flight failure catalog\n6. **Last 3 files in `memory/sessions/`** — recent context\n7. **`session-plans/pending/<active-plan>.md`** — current plan\n8. **Relevant constitution files** as task demands (don't load all every session)\n9. **Relevant skills + agents + commands** as task demands\n\n---\n\n## Anti-Patterns to Avoid\n\n(From `memory/patterns-discovered/SYNTHESIS.md` § 6, full catalog 23 items. Highest-priority for this directory:)\n\n- **AP-1 Same-agent self-review** — never review your own implementation; dispatch fresh-context verifier\n- **AP-2 Self-track wind-down** — `.transcript-tokens` real-transcript is authoritative, not LLM self-track\n- **AP-5 Charter-coherence defer overriding user-CRITICAL** — re-read all `user_prompt/*` at every phase entry; never silently defer USER-CRITICAL\n- **AP-7 Performative SC ticking** — defer with explicit prerequisites > fire vacuous proposals\n- **AP-8 Pre-staged work causing checkpoint drift** — update `current-execution.md` immediately on task complete, not session-end\n- **AP-17 Identity drift** — stockforge is AI-first VN stock advisory; not generic financial framework (see `constitution/identity-scope.md` once Track 7 ships)\n- **AP-23 Continuous LLM-Guardian** — deterministic hooks = Guardian; LLM Guardian only at session-end aggregation\n\n---\n\n## Connection to human-workspace/\n\nThis directory is the agent's domain. Human's domain is `human-workspace/`. The two communicate through:\n- Human → Agent: `human-workspace/user_prompt/`, `human-workspace/decisions/`\n- Agent → Human: `human-workspace/notifications/`, `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/`\n- Bidirectional: `human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/` (agent writes pending; human moves answered)\n- Audit trail: this directory's `memory/decisions/` references `human-workspace/` source files via path pointers\n\nAgent never writes to `human-workspace/` outside the designated `q-and-a/pending/` channel.\n","contentDiffersFromDisk":false},"displayPath":"agent-workspace\\CLAUDE.md"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"b53b886d-cdb1-444e-b9bc-b6888e3a71a8","timestamp":"2026-04-29T13:27:42.946Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"c663f411-7a8e-4679-be93-87cad134db31","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"d31a39c2-b040-46ad-9e2b-9dfab902578b","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"9b2ded44-6e0f-408b-98de-efdd0c3aa99c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01WnkKUrC9cpoinvQZvw7o3Y","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t1. một số điều tôi nhận ra sau khi làm \"orch\":\n2\t1.1. cần phân biệt rõ ràng workspace dành cho human và agent, với cấu trúc rõ ràng, clear và provenance tracking được.\n3\t- đây là điều tôi muốn làm rõ khi thực hiện autonomous coding tại dự án stockforge này, nhiệm vụ của con người phải rõ ràng, tất cả những gì liên quan đến scope, objective goals, phải do con người quyết định \"decision\".\n4\t- đây có thể là những mục tiêu \"mơ hồ\", không rõ ràng, điều này phụ thuộc vào cách con người mô tả nó khi prompt, nhưng vẫn là layer cao nhất tác động tới ai agent.\n5\t- ai agent có thể tự quyết định những \"decision\" của ai agent, miễn là dựa trên việc \"respect\" những \"human decision\".\n6\t- vì vậy, từ các \"user prompt\", ai agent trước hết phải bóc tách được ra, rằng người dùng đang muốn chỉnh sửa scope phải không, họ đang hỏi, yêu cầu ý kiến, hay đã có quyết định, mức độ quan trọng như nào, etc...\n7\tnhững \"decision\" cấp cao này, ai agent phải tiến hành \"hỏi đáp\" lại người dùng trước khi \"tracking provenance\" chúng.\n8\t=> main session nơi chạy session claude code chính, phải có model và effort đủ để hiểu được việc này, phải delegate được tới \"context agent\", nơi phụ trách quản lý các quyết định, kiến trúc, cấu hình, spec, drift, phạm vi ảnh hưởng, etc...\n9\t- ví dụ như trong quá trình code \"orch\", human nhiều lần \"phát sinh ý tưởng\" thậm chí conflict với cả project charter ban đầu, nhưng agent không verify lại, không q&a lại, mà \"luôn chiều theo ý của người dùng\", nên project thậm chí drift ở cấp độ project charter, cao hơn cả drift scope hay session.\n10\t=> với workflow full autonomous, việc detect human input này càng quan trọng hơn cả, nhất là khi dự án trải qua nhiều phase, accumulate drift từ implementation/execution, tracking, scope... sẽ khiến dự án sai rất sai. nên mỗi khi user manual intervent, dù bằng prompt thông thường với claude code qua remote control, hay qua user_prompt file trực tiếp, thì cũng luôn chú ý và cảnh giác, để làm sao cho:\n11\t- hiểu được mục đích, mong muốn cuối cùng của người dùng là gì?\n12\t- scope, objective goals đó có cần \"human decision\" nào không, người dùng đã hiểu hết được phạm vi ảnh hưởng của chúng chưa?\n13\t- những phương án nào là khả thi, hoặc không khả thi, đánh giá độ rủi ro/reward, để người dùng cân nhắc và lựa chọn, etc...\n14\t- khi cần những quyết định ở cấp độ cao, agent sẽ \"notify\" cho human qua channel (telegram) kèm theo summary, ảnh hưởng và option suggest, recommend, để đẩy nhanh quá trình ra quyết định. còn hầu hết khi agent đã đạt được trạng thái \"sync\" với human về mặt nhận thức dự án, nó có thể tự đánh giá và quyết định.\n15\t1.2. từ 1.1, thì sau đó agent và human sẽ dần đạt được trước hết là \"chung language\", chung \"domain ubiquitous\", sau đó là chung \"design system thinking\", và cuối cùng là chung \"scope, objective goals\", khi mà ai agent thực sự hiểu được mong muốn cuối cùng của người dùng, đằng sau mỗi mô tả, mỗi chức năng, mỗi phản hồi, để từ đó góp ý và đề xuất ngược lại cho người dùng.\n16\t- tính năng này là một cấp độ cao hơn của \"/grill me\", và cần đạt phát triển một cách ưu tiên, vì khi ai agent thực sự có đủ context input ở cấp độ tương đương với human, thì với khả năng suy luận và khả năng loop/self-upgrade của chúng, việc full autonomous sẽ chỉ là phần hệ quả kéo theo đơn giản.\n17\t1.3. tất nhiên bản chất llm vẫn là llm, với đầy xác suất và rủi ro (như hacillunation hay context length limit, loss in the middle, etc...) nên human vẫn phải luôn cố gắng human-in-the-loop nhiều nhất có thể với những thông tin ở cấp độ đó.\n18\t- từ đó tôi mới đề cao hơn nhu cầu tracking và provenance, tại sao ai agent lại đưa ra quyết định đó, nó được trace ngược lại về human decision nào, đã hỏi ý kiến người dùng chưa, người dùng đã verify chưa, các cấp độ level của decision là gì, đánh giá như nào, khi nào thì cần can thiệp, khả năng tự phát hiện agent drift và human drift, etc...\n19\t- không có provenance một cách có hệ thống, khi dự án đi càng xa, khả năng trace ngược lại của cả ai agent và human càng kém. human khi phải đối mặt với hàng chục spec/document mới, session logs, learning knowledge và agent notes dày đặc trong nhiều phase autonomous, thì bản thân công việc đó đã là quá tải nếu không được sắp xếp một cách khóa học.\n20\t- spec-driven development vẫn còn nhiều bài toán cần phải xử lý, nhưng tư duy về cách tiếp cận của nó, kết hợp với obsidian vault, dựa trên ý tưởng \"karpathy agent wiki\" có thể là một hướng đi tốt, với \"human workspace\" và \"agent workspace\" rõ ràng, tự quản lý.\n21\tthông thường human sẽ chỉ cần làm việc với q&a từ agent, agent sẽ tự động sắp xếp và triển khai dựa trên chúng, agent cũng tự sync các trạng thái phát triển, các quyết định của nó cho human theo dõi nếu cần.\n22\thuman cũng có một obsidian vault trực quan, được thể hiện và link với nhau một cách rõ ràng, đầy đủ. từ vault, họ nên xem được đầy đủ thông tin của human và agent, về spec, note, prompt, decision, learning knowledge, research, plan, session, task, etc...\n23\t=> tôi tin tưởng đây là một xu hướng đúng, khi mà \"sự tin tưởng\" giữa human và agent ngày càng lớn, sẽ thực hiện autonomous coding tại dự án stockforge này, nhiệm vụ của con người phải rõ ràng, tất cả những gì liên quan đến scope, objective goals, phải do con người quyết định \"decision\".\n- đây có thể là những mục tiêu \"mơ hồ\", không rõ ràng, điều này phụ thuộc vào cách con người mô tả nó khi prompt, nhưng vẫn là layer cao nhất tác động tới ai agent.\n- ai agent có thể tự quyết định những vẫn là câu chuyện self-learning và self-upgrade nhưng deep-dive hơn:\n2\t- không giống như câu chuyện runtime, nơi llm trực tiếp \"live\" xử lý user prompt hoặc task, phải tìm được đúng context, inject context cho subagent, follow workflow, đọc được đúng spec, đọc được đúng file code, etc... \n3\tnơi cần kết quả của các bước \"indexing\", \"caching\" layer từ trước, bài toán nặng hơn về \"read\" và \"reasoning\", \"delegating\" để khiến việc runtime trở nên hiệu quả và tiết kiệm nhất có thể.\n4\t- thì self-learning/upgrade lại nặng về bài toán \"write\", \"index\", \"cache\", nơi mà thu thập càng nhiều dữ liệu (thông tin, context, event, tool call, reasoning, decision...) từ harness, từ runtime nhiều nhất có thể, với chi phí rẻ nhất mà không làm ảnh hưởng tới runtime.\n5\t=> tương tự bài toán \"read/write\" (caching/cache invalidate) truyền thống của backend engineering, thì chúng ta phải tận dụng mọi kênh thu thập data với chi phí và ảnh hưởng rẻ nhất, rồi kết hợp các background job đằng sau (có thể trigger qua hook định kì với tracking, hoặc sử dụng các tool mining knowledge bên ngoài với tốc độ indexing nhanh và cơ chế rag query chính xác hơn, tiết kiệm hơn.\n6\t=> chúng tự xử lý data, mining, phân loại, etl, dễ dàng tạo thành các \"deterministic step\", rồi có thể kết hợp với llm, để tạo thành các workflow tách biệt với runtime, chuyên phân tích và cải thiện hệ thống, nhất là hệ thống harness, agent config/settings.\n7\tkết hợp với idea của karpathy autoresearch, các repo opensource trending và hiệu quả trên github, điều này hoàn toàn có thể mang lại hiệu quả lâu dài, quan trọng là phải tìm ra các cách kết hợp deterministic/llm giống như runtime, để tối ưu chi phí và hiệu quả.\n8\t=> thêm sớm vào plan để có đủ data đo lường, tracking từ sớm. cũng phải chia boundary rõ ràng về khả năng tiếp cận data, đâu là data để phục vụ cho quá trình \"write\"/caching/indexing, tránh runtime load nhầm phải những data này (với size có thể rât lớn, mà không hiệu quả), việc cô lập và tách biệt các kho data này phải được thiết kế từ đầu, coi harnessing engineering giống như backend engineering/data etl.\n9\t=> hoàn toàn có thể tiếp cận theo hướng nhiều dữ liệu (thông tin, context, event, tool call, reasoning, decision...) từ harness, từ runtime nhiều nhất có thể, với chi phí rẻ nhất mà không làm ảnh hưởng tới runtime.\n=> tương tự bài toán {"parentUuid":"5ed47a52-0f59-4a4c-b8bb-16982d7becf2","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"nested_memory","path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\human-workspace\\CLAUDE.md","content":{"path":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge\\human-workspace\\CLAUDE.md","type":"Project","content":"# human-workspace/ — Contract\n\n> **Audience**: agents reading anything inside `human-workspace/`.\n> **Established**: Decision 002 § Track 1 (Workspace Dualism Foundation).\n\n## Identity\n\n`human-workspace/` is the **human-authored authority** layer. Everything here represents **human decisions, scope, intent, and verification**. Agents READ this directory as authoritative; agents do NOT WRITE here except in one designated channel (`q-and-a/pending/` — where agents post questions for human to answer).\n\nThis separation exists because of a failure mode observed in the orch sister project (orch `decisions/040`, post-mortem CF-DOGFOOD-2): when human and agent share a single workspace without contract, agent silently overrides human-CRITICAL items via technical-defer logic. The user explicitly raised this concern in `human-workspace/user_prompt/20260429_02_init.txt` §1.1.\n\n---\n\n## Subdirectories\n\n| Path | Purpose | Who writes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `user_prompt/` | Human's mid-flight scope/idea drops. Naming: `YYYYMMDD_NN_<slug>.txt`. Files are immutable post-creation (audit trail). | **Human only**. Agent: read-only. |\n| `decisions/` | Human's strategic decisions (e.g., scope-lock, charter-revision-trigger, peer-share authorization). Format: `D-H-<NNN>-<slug>.md`. | **Human only**. Agent: read-only. |\n| `q-and-a/pending/` | **The ONE channel where agent writes inside human-workspace**. Agent drops Q&A bundles per Grill Maximization doctrine; human responds inline or moves to `answered/`. | **Both** (agent writes new bundles; human writes answers). |\n| `q-and-a/answered/` | Q&A bundles human has answered (with answers inline). Agent reads answers and acts. Archive forever; provenance trail. | **Human moves** (drag from `pending/`); agent reads. |\n| `q-and-a/stale/` | Pending bundles that exceeded their `expected_answer_by` (default 24h, urgent 4h). Auto-moved by SessionStart hook (Track 5). | **Hook moves**; both read. |\n| `notifications/` | Agent push to human — summaries, alerts, milestones. Format: `N-<TS>-<level>-<slug>.md`. Levels: INFO / SUMMARY / ALERT. | **Agent writes**; human reads. |\n\n---\n\n## Contract Rules (BINDING)\n\n1. **Agent NEVER writes to `user_prompt/` or `decisions/`.** Permission deny. If something feels like a human decision but the human hasn't written it, dispatch a Q&A bundle into `q-and-a/pending/` instead.\n\n2. **`user_prompt/` files are immutable post-creation.** Agent never deletes, renames, or edits these files. They are the audit trail of human interventions.\n\n3. **Q&A bundle format** (per Track 4 spec): YAML frontmatter (`id`, `topic`, `opened_at`, `expected_answer_by`, `priority`, `related_decisions`, `status`) + question body + answer-fill section. Each bundle = up to 25 questions per Grill Maximization doctrine; split if more.\n\n4. **Agent does not move files between `q-and-a/{pending,answered,stale}/`** — that's human's role (or hook's, in case of stale). Agent only WRITES new pending bundles and READS answers.\n\n5. **Notifications are read-only for human.** Human shouldn't edit `notifications/*` files; if disagreement with notification content, drop a `user_prompt/` instead. Notifications are the agent's account of events.\n\n6. **Provenance pointers**: every `agent-workspace/memory/decisions/D-<NNN>` should reference its source `human-workspace/user_prompt/<file>` or `human-workspace/decisions/D-H-<NNN>` if the agent's decision derives from human input.\n\n7. **No multi-tenancy in this directory.** Per identity-scope.md (Track 7), stockforge is single-tenant Phase 0-5; if peer share happens it's via git-fork, each peer has their own `human-workspace/` per fork.\n\n---\n\n## Reading Priority for Agent\n\nWhen loading session context (per `agent-workspace/constitution/autonomous-protocol.md` Track 7):\n\n1. **All `user_prompt/*.txt`** — every prompt, not just most recent. Per orch lesson (decision-040 USER-CRITICAL tier): never silently defer human-CRITICAL items.\n2. **All `decisions/*.md`** — human's strategic decisions are above charter principles in priority; charter is below human (charter was authored by human in the first place).\n3. **Latest `q-and-a/answered/*`** — recent answers update agent's understanding.\n4. **Open `q-and-a/pending/*`** — flag if waiting on human answers.\n5. **Recent `notifications/*`** (last 7 days) — for situational awareness.\n\n---\n\n## Agent Self-Check\n\nBefore writing to `human-workspace/q-and-a/pending/`, ask:\n- Is this question genuinely something the human must decide? (Charter principle / Charter-affecting / SCOPE-affecting / above ARCH-tier confidence threshold)\n- Have I already grilled this in a recent bundle? (Don't ask twice; don't pollute pending/)\n- Am I bundling per Grill Maximization (target 15-20 questions, max 25)? Or splintering across many small bundles?\n\nIf the answer to any is \"I'm not sure\" — DON'T write the bundle. Either answer it yourself with charter-principle reasoning + log decision, or wait until ambiguity clears.\n","contentDiffersFromDisk":false},"displayPath":"human-workspace\\CLAUDE.md"},"type":"attachment","uuid":"6b0082d8-5ff5-4f19-b31b-0d47d0577a89","timestamp":"2026-04-29T13:28:31.527Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"C:\\htdocs\\stockforge","sessionId":"c663f411-7a8e-4679-be93-87cad134db31","version":"2.1.122","gitBranch":"main"}

No auto-revival.\n100\t\n101\ttags: [\"phase-0\", \"scope\", \"orch-port\", \"knowledge-crystal\"]\n102\t---\n103\t\n104\t# Decision 001 — Orch vs Claude Code Native: Pause Orch, Port Patterns\n105\t\n106\t> Status promoted from PROPOSED → ACCEPTED on 2026-04-29 via Round 1+2 Q&A audit. See `human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/2026-04-29-001-phase0-clusters.md`.\n107\t\n108\t---\n109\t\n110\t## Context\n111\t\n112\tThe user authored Orch (`C:\\htdocs\\orch-starter`) as a side project to manage the autonomous Claude Code coding loop for StockForge. Through 12+ phases, 36+ sessions, and 5 user-prompt interventions (`tasks/feat_01..feat_05`), Orch reached v2.2.0 with 1,470/1,470 tests passing and charter criteria F1-F8, N1-N5, O1-O4, S1-S4 all PASS.\n113\t\n114\tDuring Orch's own development, Claude Code (April 2026) shipped capabilities that overlap heavily with Orch's value proposition:\n115\t\n116\t- Subagent dispatch (`Agent` tool with `subagent_type` + `run_in_background`)\n117\t- Mobile remote control (`--rc` flag + claude.ai mobile app)\n118\t- Native skills with progressive disclosure\n119\t- Hooks (SessionStart/SessionEnd/Stop/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/SubagentStop/UserPromptSubmit)\n120\t- Scheduled execution (CronCreate, ScheduleWakeup, /loop skill)\n121\t- Plan mode (EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode)\n122\t- Worktree isolation per agent (EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree)\n123\t- Native task tracking (TaskCreate/Update/List)\n124\t- /effort modes (low/medium/high/xhigh/max)\n125\t\n126\tThe user's question (translated): \"Should I continue developing Orch as a tool to support StockForge, or has Claude Code's native system become good enough that Orch is unnecessary for personal use? If unnecessary, what should I port from Orch into StockForge to achieve full-autonomous coding?\"\n127\t\n128\t---\n129\t\n130\t## Analysis\n131\t\n132\t### What Orch uniquely offers\n133\t\n134\t| Capability | Status in CC native | Verdict for stockforge |\n135\t|---|---|---|\n136\t| Multi-project queue dispatch (1 daemon → N projects) | Not native | **Overkill** — stockforge is the only project |\n137\t| Auto ccs profile failover on rate-limit | Not native | **Replaceable by bash hook** (~50 LOC) |\n138\t| OTEL aggregation across sessions | `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` exists; no aggregator | **Replaceable by local JSONL logging** |\n139\t| Telegram bot interface | claude.ai mobile + `--rc` covers it | **Fully replaced** |\n140\t| Web UI dashboard (kanban, live tail, cost chart) | Not native | **Nice-to-have, not blocker** for solo use |\n141\t| Token-based auto-reboot via keystroke injection | Not native | **Port script directly** (`session-self-reboot.sh`) |\n142\t| Auto-resume from checkpoint after reboot | Not native | **Port pattern** (SessionStart hook reads `checkpoints/latest.md`) |\n143\t| Loop-resilience guards (Mode A/B/C) | Not native | **Port hooks directly** (3 small bash scripts) |\n144\t\n145\t### What CC native handles that Orch had to build\n146\t\n147\t- Subagent dispatch — CC has this natively, no daemon needed\n148\t- Skills with progressive disclosure\n149\t- Hooks pipeline\n150\t- Scheduling primitives\n151\t- Remote interaction\n152\t- Single-project task tracking\n153\t\n154\t### Cost-benefit of continuing Orch development\n155\t\n156\t**Costs of continuing:**\n157\t- Phases 8-12+ (self-application bootstrap) require ongoing autonomous sessions on Orch itself\n158\t- Every Orch session costs tokens that could go into StockForge\n159\t- Maintenance burden compounds (1,470 tests to keep green)\n160\t- Drift surface area is now larger than the value-add over CC native\n161\t\n162\t**Benefits of continuing:**\n163\t- Phase 1.7 vision (community/SaaS direction) — only realized if user actively pursues team-share path\n164\t- Knowledge crystal — patterns learned through real autonomous execution\n165\t\n166\t**Verdict on cost-benefit:** For solo personal use on StockForge alone, the marginal value of continuing Orch is low and the marginal cost is real. The community/SaaS path remains valid as a SEPARATE FUTURE TRACK, but should not block StockForge's own autonomous coding loop.\n167\t\n168\t---\n169\t\n170\t## Decision\n171\t\n172\t**PAUSE active Orch development. PORT the proven patterns into StockForge as scripts/skills/agents/constitution updates. KEEP Orch as a knowledge-crystal repo (read-only reference) and a optional future track for community/SaaS sharing.**\n173\t\n174\t### What \"pause\" means concretely\n175\t\n176\t- Do NOT continue Phase 8+ in Orch\n177\t- Do NOT spawn sessions to add features to Orch\n178\t- Do NOT delete Orch — it's a reference and a future-revival option\n179\t- Cap Orch sessions at: incidental bug fixes IF used as reference; otherwise read-only\n180\t\n181\t### What \"port\" means concretely\n182\t\n183\tSee companion document: `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/001-port-from-orch.md`. No auto-revival.\n\ntags: [\"phase-0\", \"scope\", \"orch-port\", \"knowledge-crystal\"]\n---\n\n# Decision 001 — Orch vs Claude Code Native: Pause Orch, Port Patterns\n\n> Status promoted from PROPOSED → ACCEPTED on 2026-04-29 via Round 1+2 Q&A audit. See `human-workspace/q-and-a/answered/2026-04-29-001-phase0-clusters.md`.\n\n---\n\n## Context\n\nThe user authored Orch (`C:\\htdocs\\orch-starter`) as a side project to manage the autonomous Claude Code coding loop for StockForge. Through 12+ phases, 36+ sessions, and 5 user-prompt interventions (`tasks/feat_01..feat_05`), Orch reached v2.2.0 with 1,470/1,470 tests passing and charter criteria F1-F8, N1-N5, O1-O4, S1-S4 all PASS.\n\nDuring Orch's own development, Claude Code (April 2026) shipped capabilities that overlap heavily with Orch's value proposition:\n\n- Subagent dispatch (`Agent` tool with `subagent_type` + `run_in_background`)\n- Mobile remote control (`--rc` flag + claude.ai mobile app)\n- Native skills with progressive disclosure\n- Hooks (SessionStart/SessionEnd/Stop/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/SubagentStop/UserPromptSubmit)\n- Scheduled execution (CronCreate, ScheduleWakeup, /loop skill)\n- Plan mode (EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode)\n- Worktree isolation per agent (EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree)\n- Native task tracking (TaskCreate/Update/List)\n- /effort modes (low/medium/high/xhigh/max)\n\nThe user's question (translated): \"Should I continue developing Orch as a tool to support StockForge, or has Claude Code's native system become good enough that Orch is unnecessary for personal use? If unnecessary, what should I port from Orch into StockForge to achieve full-autonomous coding?\"\n\n---\n\n## Analysis\n\n### What Orch uniquely offers\n\n| Capability | Status in CC native | Verdict for stockforge |\n|---|---|---|\n| Multi-project queue dispatch (1 daemon → N projects) | Not native | **Overkill** — stockforge is the only project |\n| Auto ccs profile failover on rate-limit | Not native | **Replaceable by bash hook** (~50 LOC) |\n| OTEL aggregation across sessions | `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` exists; no aggregator | **Replaceable by local JSONL logging** |\n| Telegram bot interface | claude.ai mobile + `--rc` covers it | **Fully replaced** |\n| Web UI dashboard (kanban, live tail, cost chart) | Not native | **Nice-to-have, not blocker** for solo use |\n| Token-based auto-reboot via keystroke injection | Not native | **Port script directly** (`session-self-reboot.sh`) |\n| Auto-resume from checkpoint after reboot | Not native | **Port pattern** (SessionStart hook reads `checkpoints/latest.md`) |\n| Loop-resilience guards (Mode A/B/C) | Not native | **Port hooks directly** (3 small bash scripts) |\n\n### What CC native handles that Orch had to build\n\n- Subagent dispatch — CC has this natively, no daemon needed\n- Skills with progressive disclosure\n- Hooks pipeline\n- Scheduling primitives\n- Remote interaction\n- Single-project task tracking\n\n### Cost-benefit of continuing Orch development\n\n**Costs of continuing:**\n- Phases 8-12+ (self-application bootstrap) require ongoing autonomous sessions on Orch itself\n- Every Orch session costs tokens that could go into StockForge\n- Maintenance burden compounds (1,470 tests to keep green)\n- Drift surface area is now larger than the value-add over CC native\n\n**Benefits of continuing:**\n- Phase 1.7 vision (community/SaaS direction) — only realized if user actively pursues team-share path\n- Knowledge crystal — patterns learned through real autonomous execution\n\n**Verdict on cost-benefit:** For solo personal use on StockForge alone, the marginal value of continuing Orch is low and the marginal cost is real. The community/SaaS path remains valid as a SEPARATE FUTURE TRACK, but should not block StockForge's own autonomous coding loop.\n\n---\n\n## Decision\n\n**PAUSE active Orch development. PORT the proven patterns into StockForge as scripts/skills/agents/constitution updates. KEEP Orch as a knowledge-crystal repo (read-only reference) and a optional future track for community/SaaS sharing.**\n\n### What \"pause\" means concretely\n\n- Do NOT continue Phase 8+ in Orch\n- Do NOT spawn sessions to add features to Orch\n- Do NOT delete Orch — it's a reference and a future-revival option\n- Cap Orch sessions at: incidental bug fixes IF used as reference; otherwise read-only\n\n### What \"port\" means concretely\n\nSee companion document: `agent-workspace/session-plans/pending/001-port-from-orch.md`. Summary of port categories:\n\n1. **Hook scripts** (highest leverage, 7 scripts) — budget-watchdog, autonomous-stop-watchdog, dispatch-jsonl-recorder, session-start-bootstrap, component-telemetry, subagent-stop-logger, tool-call-first-lint\n2. **Reboot scripts** — session-self-reboot.sh + .ps1 (keystroke injection at 200K/230K thresholds)\n3. **Discipline skills** (7 skills) — subagent-driven-development, verification-before-completion, systematic-debugging, research-first, brainstorming, confusion-protocol, spawned-session-mode, observation-file-write-on-return\n4. **Subagents** (5 new) — task-implementer, spec-compliance-reviewer, code-quality-reviewer, systematic-debugger, research-scanner, telemetry-analyst\n5. **Commands** (5 new) — context-save, context-restore, phase-advance, harness-audit, invariant-check\n6. **Constitution files** (3 new) — autonomous-protocol, model-routing, research-protocol; merge reusability-rules content into stockforge's existing files\n7. **Memory infrastructure** — checkpoints/, decisions/, escalation.md, .transcript-tokens, .wind-down marker, .autonomous-stop-watchdog.log\n8. **CLAUDE.md additions** — Budget Watchdog Protocol, Autonomous Mode + STOP conditions, Self-reboot mechanics, Tool-call-first ordering, Modes A/B/C defense\n\n### What NOT to port\n\n- `packages/core/` — TypeScript/NestJS daemon. StockForge is Python-primary; adapter pattern not needed for single-project.\n- `apps/web` — React Web UI dashboard. Solo use → claude.ai mobile is enough.\n- `apps/telegram` — Telegram bot. Replaced by `--rc`.\n- Multi-project profile.yaml machinery. Overkill.\n- `scripts/audit/n6-72h-*.sh`, `scripts/audit/oss-readiness.sh`, etc. — OSS-readiness audits irrelevant for personal stockforge use.\n\n---\n\n## Why (Reasons)\n\n1. **Charter principle \"Tight scope\"** — Orch was scoped as orchestrator, but for solo single-project use the orchestration value is now mostly absorbed by CC native.\n2. **Karpathy P2 (Simplicity First)** — running Orch as a daemon adds 1 process + 1 SQLite + 1 NestJS server + 1 React UI to keep alive, in exchange for capabilities that scripts in stockforge/scripts/ can deliver in ~500 LOC.\n3. **Karpathy P3 (Surgical Changes)** — porting only the patterns that actually move the needle (hooks, reboot, skills) is a smaller change than maintaining Orch.\n4. **User's own observation** (translated, feat_05): \"the cost of each reboot is too high to continue prior work… memory/notes/learning have grown to expensive levels.\" Solving this is a stockforge-internal optimization, not an orch feature.\n5. **Drift control** — Orch's 7+ phases revealed that drift is severe even with great configs. The drift-control mechanisms (drift-check, harness-audit, post-phase verifier) are pattern-level learnings; baking them into stockforge directly is more reliable than indirecting through orch.\n\n---\n\n## Risks & Mitigations\n\n| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |\n|---|---|---|\n| User changes mind, wants Orch for team-share later | Medium | Keep Orch repo intact; revival is `git pull` away |\n| Some ported pattern doesn't fit stockforge's Python-primary stack | Low | Hooks/scripts are bash; skills are markdown; subagents are markdown — all framework-agnostic |\n| CC native ships a regression that orch had a workaround for | Low | Hooks intercept the same boundaries; workarounds port directly |\n| Porting takes longer than expected | Medium | Phase the port: priority 1 (loop-resilience), priority 2 (skills), priority 3 (subagents/commands) |\n| New Orch insights missed by stopping development | Low | Knowledge through phases 0-7 is already crystallized in `agent-workspace/`; no expected breakthrough in phase 8+ |\n\n---\n\n## Outcomes\n\nIf user confirms:\n1. Orch development paused; mark as \"reference repo\" with a note in its README\n2. Execute port roadmap (`session-plans/pending/001-port-from-orch.md`) over 3-5 autonomous sessions\n3. The user observed in UP02 §1.1: \"agent không verify lại, không q&a lại, mà luôn chiều theo ý của người dùng, nên project thậm chí drift ở cấp độ project charter.\" This is a charter-level drift observation that informs the entire design.\n212\t\n213\t---\n214\t\n215\t## Decision\n216\t\n217\t**Phase 0 = Harness Bootstrap = 10 tracks, executed in supervised mode until Track 7 completes (then autonomous mode activates).**\n218\t\n219\t### Phase numbering update (this decision)\n220\t\n221\t| Old | New | Description |\n222\t|---|---|---|\n223\t| — | **Phase 0 (NEW)** | Harness Bootstrap |\n224\t| Phase 0 | Phase 1 | Project Setup (Day 1 Checklist) |\n225\t| Phase 1 | Phase 2 | Foundation (Tier 1+2 ingestion) |\n226\t| Phase 2 | Phase 3 | Edge Sources (Tier 3+4) |\n227\t| Phase 3 | Phase 4 | Multi-perspective adversarial agents |\n228\t| Phase 4 | Phase 5 | Compounding outer loop |\n229\t\n230\tUpdated in `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` + `current-execution.md` (this turn). `CLAUDE.md` references will be updated in Track 7.\n231\t\n232\t---\n233\t\n234\t## Track Specifications\n235\t\n236\t### Track 0 — Pattern Mining (3 sources, parallel)\n237\t- **Goal**: Extract BORROW / ADAPT / LEARN / SKIP patterns from 3 evidence sources before designing remaining tracks\n238\t- **Sources**: \n239\t  1. The user observed in UP02 §1.1: \"agent không verify lại, không q&a lại, mà luôn chiều theo ý của người dùng, nên project thậm chí drift ở cấp độ project charter.\" This is a charter-level drift observation that informs the entire design.\n\n---\n\n## Decision\n\n**Phase 0 = Harness Bootstrap = 10 tracks, executed in supervised mode until Track 7 completes (then autonomous mode activates).**\n\n### Phase numbering update (this decision)\n\n| Old | New | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| — | **Phase 0 (NEW)** | Harness Bootstrap |\n| Phase 0 | Phase 1 | Project Setup (Day 1 Checklist) |\n| Phase 1 | Phase 2 | Foundation (Tier 1+2 ingestion) |\n| Phase 2 | Phase 3 | Edge Sources (Tier 3+4) |\n| Phase 3 | Phase 4 | Multi-perspective adversarial agents |\n| Phase 4 | Phase 5 | Compounding outer loop |\n\nUpdated in `agent-workspace/memory/project.md` + `current-execution.md` (this turn). `CLAUDE.md` references will be updated in Track 7.\n\n---\n\n## Track Specifications\n\n### Track 0 — Pattern Mining (3 sources, parallel)\n- **Goal**: Extract BORROW / ADAPT / LEARN / SKIP patterns from 3 evidence sources before designing remaining tracks\n- **Sources**: \n  1. Orch knowledge crystal: `C:\\htdocs\\orch-starter\\agent-workspace\\memory\\decisions\\` + `agent-notes.md` + `phase-N-complete.md` (1..7) + `post-mortems\\`\n  2. ms-mdp-admin phase2_workflow: `C:\\htdocs\\labci\\ms-mdp-admin_refactor\\tasks\\refactor_phase2\\phase2_workflow\\` (38 docs; deep-read 10, skim rest)\n  3. Orch reference-repos: `C:\\htdocs\\orch-starter\\reference-repos\\` + existing notes in `C:\\htdocs\\orch-starter\\agent-workspace\\research\\`\n- **Mechanism**: 3 general-purpose agents in `run_in_background: true`, parallel\n- **Output**: 3 files in `agent-workspace/memory/patterns-discovered/pattern-mining-{orch,msmdp,refrepos}.md` + `SYNTHESIS.md` + `borrow-list.md`\n- **Synthesis step**: separate opus agent (fresh context) reads 3 mining reports, produces `SYNTHESIS.md` + `borrow-list.md`\n- **Dependency**: none (kicks off immediately, parallel with Tracks 1-2 if possible)\n- **Est tokens**: 3 × 50K (parallel, bg) + 30K synthesis = ~180K\n- **Success**: 5 files produced; each pattern categorized; synthesis identifies top-20 BORROW + adaptations needed for stockforge Python stack\n- **Risk**: Subagent doesn't comply with output schema → mitigation: explicit output structure in prompt + verifier\n\n### Track 1 — Workspace Dualism Foundation\n- **Goal**: Establish folder contract between human-workspace/ and agent-workspace/; profile card auto-generated; agent's next session reads profile cards before dispatching subagents (model routing influenced)\n\n---\n\n## Sequencing & Dependencies\n\n```\nTrack 0 (background, parallel)              [start immediately]\n  ├─ orch mining (~50K, bg)\n  ├─ msmdp mining (~50K, bg)\n  └─ refrepos mining (~50K, bg)\n  → Synthesis (~30K, opus, fresh)            [after all 3 return]\n\nTrack 1 (foundation)                          [in parallel with Track 0 if budget allows]\n  └─ Track 2 (provenance)\n       ├─ Track 3 (intent classifier)\n       └─ Track 4 (Q&A escalation)\n\nTrack 5 (loop-resilience hooks)               [parallel with Track 3-4 OK]\n  └─ Track 6 (skills + subagents)\n       └─ Track 7 (constitution + CLAUDE.md)\n            └─ AUTONOMOUS_MODE activated\n\nTrack 8 (Confidence Score)                    [needs 4, 5]\nTrack 9 (Self-Awareness)                      [needs 5]\n```\n\nRecommended session breakdown (Q&A E4 = B confirmed: sequential per cluster + verifier subagent + user reviews final each cluster):\n\n| Session | Tracks | Type | Budget |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| S1 | Dispatch Track 0 (bg) + Tracks 1, 2 | FOCUSED_IMPL | 100K main + 180K bg |\n| S2 | Track 0 synthesis + Track 3 + Track 4 | MULTI_TASK_IMPL | 150K |\n| S3 | Track 5 | FOCUSED_IMPL | 100K |\n| S4 | Track 6 | MULTI_TASK_IMPL (subagent-driven) | 200K (heavy) |\n| S5 | Track 7 + verifier on Tracks 1-6 | VERIFY+IMPL | 130K |\n| S6 | Track 8 | FOCUSED_IMPL | 130K |\n| S7 | Track 9 + final verifier | VERIFY+IMPL | 130K |\n\nTotal: ~940K main + 180K bg = ~1.1M tokens.\n\n---\n\n## Risk & Mitigation\n\n| Risk | Mitigation |\n|---|---|\n| Track 0 agents return low-quality mining (subagent context bias) | Explicit output schema + verifier reads after; User specifically observed that \"sync questions\" between human-LLM about *intent* of harness configuration are missing.\n145\t2. **Layer separation** — clear division between harness (reusable across projects), agent-workspace, human-workspace, project-specific. Foundation for \"context injection\" + portability (e.g., `/attach <new-project>`).\n146\t3. **Self-upgrade / Self-test** — Karpathy autoresearch loop style: measure → trace → evaluate → improve. Specifically requires a skill/agent that decomposes work into \"deterministic\" vs \"LLM probability\" portions.\n147\t\n148\tUser-provided directive: **\"biến việc sync thành ưu tiên hàng đầu, giúp llm trở thành second brain thực sự.\"**\n149\t\n150\t### Audit at decision time (S3 close)\n151\t\n152\t**Drift detection — present**: D1-D8 hooks (S3 ship), `/drift-check`, `drift-detector` subagent, `/ul-audit`, `charter-coherence-spot.sh`, `post-tool-citation-grep.sh`, `taskcompleted-audit.sh`.\n153\t\n154\t**Drift detection — missing**:\n155\t- \"Sync drift\" (human-LLM mutual understanding of harness intent)\n156\t- Intent-vs-implementation semantic diff (UP-NN vs current artifacts)\n157\t- Periodic auto-fired sync re-grilling (no \"you haven't asked me about X for N sessions\" trigger)\n158\t- Cross-session drift comparison\n159\t\n160\t**Layer separation — present**: workspace dualism (`human-workspace/` vs `agent-workspace/`), constitution immutable, contracts.\n161\t\n162\t**Layer separation — missing**: harness vs stockforge biz logic still entangled in `.claude/`; no manifest; no `/attach` skill; no global/personal/committed/non-committed layer rules.\n163\t\n164\t**Self-upgrade — present**: `agent-notes.md`, `patterns-discovered/`, `mistake-log` (S5), telemetry hooks, Track 9 placeholder.\n165\t\n166\t**Self-upgrade — missing**: deterministic-vs-LLM decomposer skill, capability-map artifact, Karpathy autoresearch loop framework, formal promotion path (`agent-notes` → `skill`/`hook`/`constitution`).\n167\t\n168\t---\n169\t\n170\t## Decision\n171\t\n172\t**Insert Track 5.5 between Track 5 and Track 6 of D-002 Phase 0 plan, with three sub-tracks executed Layer → Sync → Self-Cap, then rewrite Track 6 based on the new layer manifest.**\n173\t\n174\t### Sub-track 5.5a — Layer Foundation (~150K, 1 session = S4)\n175\t\n176\t**Goals**:\n177\t- Author `.claude/manifest.yaml` — schema declaring scope of each artifact (`harness` portable / `stockforge` biz-specific / `hybrid` / `personal` non-committed)\n178\t- Directory restructure: move stockforge-biz skills/agents to `.claude/stockforge/` subtree; keep portable harness skills/agents/commands in `.claude/` root\n179\t- Author `/attach` skill — copies harness layer (excluding `.claude/stockforge/`) to a target project path\n180\t- Define layer rules: global (machine-wide) / personal (user-tagged, gitignored) / committed (in-repo) / non-committed (in-repo but gitignored)\n181\t- **NOT multi-tenant** (per Round 2 Q6=D) — single human assumption; future peer-share via git-fork\n182\t\n183\t**Files affected**:\n184\t- `.claude/manifest.yaml` (NEW)\n185\t- `.claude/stockforge/skills/<biz-skill>/` (MOVE: candidates include `evidence-extraction`, `postgres-pgvector`, `crawler-reliability`, `fastapi-module`; final categorization happens in S4)\n186\t- `.claude/skills/attach/SKILL.md` + `references/` (NEW)\n187\t- `.gitignore` extended for personal/non-committed paths\n188\t- `.claude/settings.json` permissions adjusted for new paths\n189\t\n190\t**Success**: manifest validates; restructured tree passes drift-signals-D1-D8 dry-run; `/attach` smoke-test copies harness to scratch dir + reproduces working CLAUDE.md Estimate lands at ~2.02M; within accepted band.\n279\t\n280\t---\n281\t\n282\t## Why (Reasons)\n283\t\n284\t1. **UP-06 §1 directive elevation of sync is binding** (UP-NN files have higher priority than charter principles per `agent-workspace/CLAUDE.md` Reading Priority — \"decisions/*.md are above charter principles\").\n285\t\n286\t2. **Layer-first sequencing reduces refactor cost** — Track 6 (skills port) lands cleanly after manifest exists; otherwise skills move twice (once into `.claude/`, once again into `.claude/stockforge/`).\n287\t\n288\t3. **Sync 4-mechanism ensemble is defense-in-depth** — periodic grilling catches scheduled drift; intent-diff agent catches semantic drift; sync-state.md provides single-source-of-truth audit; sync Q&A template ensures questions are well-formed for \"understanding\" vs \"implementation\". Single mechanism would leave gaps.\n289\t\n290\t4. **Aggressive Karpathy autoresearch matches stockforge mission** — financial advisory requires multi-perspective + measurement-driven calibration (charter principles). The autoresearch loop framework operationalizes both.\n291\t\n292\t5. **OTEL+JSONL hybrid provides scale headroom** — JSONL alone suffices for current scale; OTEL adds standard tooling for future externalization (peer-share, cloud telemetry). Cost is ~200K one-time setup vs forever-locked-in custom.\n293\t\n294\t6. **Multi-tenant explicitly skipped** to avoid scope creep. `/attach` covers project portability; if peer-share happens later, git-fork single-tenant pattern remains cleanest.\n295\t\n296\t---\n297\t\n298\t## Risks & Mitigations\n299\t\n300\t| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |\n301\t|---|---|---|\n302\t| Track 5.5 budget overshoots ~2M | Medium | Per-session budget watchdog (Track 5 hook) auto-reboots at 80% cliff. If 5.5c overshoots, descope c.4 OTEL to \"design-only\" + defer collector docker to Track 9. |\n303\t| Layer manifest 5.5a gets entire restructure wrong → cascading rework | Medium | Smoke-test `/attach` on scratch dir BEFORE moving any production skill; sandwich-verifier dispatch (fresh ctx) on manifest before S5 starts. |\n304\t| Sync grilling hook fires too often (annoying) | Low | Configurable threshold; default 3 sessions OR 7 days OR explicit user \"sync now\" command. Easy to tune. |\n305\t| Karpathy autoresearch over-engineered for current scale | Medium | Start with `try-n-approaches` skill smoke-test on real task; if signal weak, descope OTEL to design-doc-only. |\n306\t| Multi-tenant skip creates future regret if peer-share happens | Low | Documented escape hatch: git-fork single-tenant remains valid pattern; revisit if peer-share materializes (unlikely Phase 0-5). |\n307\t| 5.5c overlap with Track 9 self-awareness creates duplicate work | Low | Track 9 budget reduced to 80K (was 120K) reflecting 5.5c absorbs OTEL setup. Track 9 retained for live profile cards + aggregator hook (separate concern). |\n308\t\n309\t---\n310\t\n311\t## Open Questions\n312\t\n313\tNone blocking S4 start. Specifically requires a skill/agent that decomposes work into \"deterministic\" vs \"LLM probability\" portions.\n\nUser-provided directive: **\"biến việc sync thành ưu tiên hàng đầu, giúp llm trở Intent-vs-implementation semantic diff (UP-NN vs current artifacts)\n- Periodic auto-fired sync re-grilling (no \"you haven't asked me about X for N sessions\" trigger)\n- Cross-session drift biz logic still entangled in `.claude/`; no manifest; no `/attach` skill; no global/personal/committed/non-committed layer rules.\n\n**Self-upgrade — present**: `agent-notes.md`, loop framework, formal promotion path (`agent-notes` → `skill`/`hook`/`constitution`).\n\n---\n\n## Decision\n\n**Insert Track 5.5 between Track 5 and Track 6 of D-002 Phase 0 plan, with three 2 Q6=D) — single human assumption; future peer-share via git-fork\n\n**Files affected**:\n- `.claude/manifest.yaml` (NEW)\n- `.claude/stockforge/skills/<biz-skill>/` (MOVE: candidates include `/attach` smoke-test copies harness to scratch dir + reproduces working CLAUDE.md skeleton.\n\n### Sub-track 5.5b — Sync Infrastructure (~300K, 2 sessions = S5+S6)\n\n**5.5b.1 — Estimate lands at ~2.02M; within accepted band.\n\n---\n\n## Why (Reasons)\n\n1. **UP-06 §1 directive elevation of sync is binding** (UP-NN files have higher priority than charter principles per `agent-workspace/CLAUDE.md` Reading Priority — \"decisions/*.md are above charter principles\").\n\n2. **Layer-first sequencing reduces refactor cost** — Track 6 (skills port) lands cleanly after manifest exists; otherwise skills move twice (once into `.claude/`, once again into `.claude/stockforge/`).\n\n3. **Sync 4-mechanism ensemble is defense-in-depth** — periodic grilling catches scheduled drift; intent-diff agent catches semantic drift; sync-state.md provides single-source-of-truth audit; sync Q&A template ensures questions are well-formed for \"understanding\" vs \"implementation\". Single mechanism would leave gaps.\n\n4. **Aggressive Karpathy autoresearch matches stockforge mission** — financial advisory requires multi-perspective + measurement-driven calibration (charter principles). The autoresearch loop framework operationalizes both.\n\n5. **OTEL+JSONL hybrid provides scale headroom** — JSONL alone suffices for current scale; OTEL adds standard tooling for future externalization (peer-share, cloud telemetry). Cost is ~200K one-time setup vs forever-locked-in custom.\n\n6. **Multi-tenant explicitly skipped** to avoid scope creep. `/attach` covers project portability; if peer-share happens later, git-fork single-tenant pattern remains cleanest.\n\n---\n\n## Risks & Mitigations\n\n| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |\n|---|---|---|\n| Track 5.5 budget overshoots ~2M | Medium | Per-session budget watchdog (Track 5 hook) auto-reboots at 80% cliff. Easy to tune. |\n| Karpathy autoresearch over-engineered for current scale | Medium | Start with `try-n-approaches` skill smoke-test on real task; if signal weak, descope OTEL to design-doc-only. |\n| Multi-tenant skip creates future regret if peer-share happens | Low | Documented escape hatch: git-fork single-tenant remains valid pattern; revisit if peer-share materializes (unlikely Phase 0-5). |\n| 5.5c overlap with Track 9 self-awareness creates duplicate work | Low | Track 9 budget reduced to 80K (was 120K) reflecting 5.5c absorbs OTEL setup.
